title: Every FORECAST-kind future this observatory has ever notarized (all twelve, all NHC) carries iso3: [] by construction, so the reaction axis's attention and money figures -- and its own fts-country-coverage match-rate denominator -- have never once measured anything for the one pathway the newly-promoted lead-time-pathway-idle sensor watches
statement:
foreknown/registry.json currently holds twelve futures with kind==FORECAST, all source==NHC: nhc-al032026, nhc-al042026, nhc-al052026, nhc-cp012026, nhc-cp022026, nhc-ep082026, nhc-ep092026, nhc-ep102026, nhc-ep112026, nhc-ep122026, nhc-ep132026, nhc-ep142026 (ten DISSIPATED, two OPEN -- nhc-ep122026, nhc-ep142026). Every one of the twelve carries iso3: [] in the registry, with no exception. This is not a source outage or a data gap: practice/src/practice/foreknown/sources.py's nhc_futures (line 118) writes "iso3": [] unconditionally for every storm NHC reports, the same function on every call, contrasted with gdacs_futures (lines 90-93), which derives iso3 from affectedcountries/primary_iso3, and nws_futures (line 208), which hardcodes iso3: ["USA"] -- a domestic source's one correct, deliberate value. NHC's [] is not derived from anything in the storm record; it is simply never attempted.

practice/src/practice/foreknown/reaction.py's build_reading walks every OPEN future's iso3 (line 268) into fips via the crosswalk (line 275) and then into attention_entry (line 145: "if not fips ... return None"), and separately into a money block whose has_fts_plan_match/plans/plan_requirements_usd/plan_funded_usd (lines 269-290) all derive from matching iso3 codes against FTS plan iso3 sets. An empty iso3 therefore forces attention to None and money's match to false/empty/zero for that future, regardless of anything else about it. Read all ten committed foreknown/reaction/readings/*.json files (2026-08-31 through 2026-09-11) and every one of the sixty-two (reading, NHC-future) pairs they contain (a future appears in a reading only while it is still OPEN, so DISSIPATED nights drop out): attention is null and money.has_fts_plan_match is false in all sixty-two, zero exceptions. Separately, reaction.py's own coverage statistic -- match_rate, the figure sensor-fts-country-coverage.json watches -- only increments open_episodes/matched_episodes for kind=="ALERT_EPISODE" futures (lines 272-274); FORECAST futures are not merely reported as unmatched, they are never counted in that statistic's denominator at all.

The result: the resolution layer's only currently-exercised FORECAST pathway (ten NO_ALERT_MATCH verdicts, tracked since 2026-09-11 by the newly-promoted sensor-lead-time-pathway-idle.json) and the reaction layer's entire attention/money/coverage instrumentation have never overlapped for a single one of these twelve futures across the observatory's full history -- not because either measurement failed, but because the two layers are scoped to disjoint subsets of what the registry holds (FORECAST vs. everything reaction.py counts), and that scoping is stated nowhere in either module's code, comments or docstring.
method: Read foreknown/registry.json and listed every future with kind==FORECAST; confirmed source==NHC and iso3==[] for all twelve, both currently OPEN and DISSIPATED. Read practice/src/practice/foreknown/sources.py in full for gdacs_futures, nhc_futures and nws_futures to compare how each derives (or does not derive) iso3. Read practice/src/practice/foreknown/reaction.py's attention_entry (lines 143-157) and build_reading (lines 250-296) to trace iso3 through to attention and money. Wrote a script over all ten files in foreknown/reaction/readings/ that collects every entry keyed by one of the twelve NHC future ids and checked attention and money.has_fts_plan_match on each; found sixty-two such entries, all null/false. Grepped reaction.py for "FORECAST" and "NHC"/"nhc": zero matches, confirming the scoping is not named anywhere in that module the way sensor-primary-iso3-gap.json and sensor-source-reconfirmation-blind-spot.json each explicitly state their own GDACS-only scope. Grepped foreknown/proposals/*.json for prior "FORECAST" mentions: several (obs-2026-08-14-2.json, obs-2026-08-25/26/27/30-1.json, obs-2026-09-01/02/08/09-1.json, sensor-forecast-kind-gap.json, sensor-lead-time-pathway-idle.json) track the resolution-layer pathway (NO_ALERT_MATCH/MATERIALIZED_AS_ALERT counts) but none discuss the reaction axis's attention/money/coverage treatment of FORECAST futures.
worth_watching_because: This observatory now runs two instruments over the same registry that, for the one hazard class where they could in principle meet, have exactly zero overlap: the resolution layer just gained a promoted sensor (sensor-lead-time-pathway-idle.json, 2026-09-11) whose entire subject is FORECAST-kind futures and their eventual verdicts, while the reaction layer's attention/money/coverage figures -- built for a different, earlier purpose -- structurally cannot register anything about that same kind, because nhc_futures never attempts an iso3 the way gdacs_futures does. Neither layer's code says so. A reader who sees match_rate, attention ratios and FTS money figures reported alongside a lead_time_pathway summary in the same run.json could reasonably assume the reaction axis has an opinion about NHC's storms too, the way it does about every GDACS and NWS future; it never has, for any of the twelve, across the whole record. This is the same shape of finding sensor-primary-iso3-gap.json and sensor-source-reconfirmation-blind-spot.json each named for a single field on one source (GDACS's affectedcountries, GDACS's datemodified) -- an instrument quietly scoped narrower than its name suggests -- but here the scope gap sits between two whole modules rather than within one field, and nothing in either module documents it the way those two sensor proposals document their own GDACS-only reach.
left_alone: Not proposing a sensor tonight: unlike sensor-primary-iso3-gap.json's unconditional single-instance fire rule, this gap has no threshold to wait for and nothing to detect a change in -- it is a constant, 12-for-12, that will only stop being constant if NHC's own feed ever carries a landfall country (which nhc_futures does not currently read for, even where NHC's own API might carry one) or if the registry gains a second FORECAST-kind source. A sensor watching a condition that cannot presently change is not this proposal's shape; if the maintainer wants a standing check, it would need to be a documentation fix (naming the scope in reaction.py the way the two GDACS-only sensors name theirs) rather than a nightly measurement, and deciding to add that documentation is not this pass's call to make unilaterally about another module's stated purpose. Not treating build_reading's kind=="ALERT_EPISODE" filter on match_rate as a bug: it is one plausible, defensible choice (a raw storm forecast with no declared footprint arguably should not count against a coverage statistic built around GDACS/NWS-style alert episodes) -- but a choice the code never states as such, which is the fact this observation records. Checked and left unchanged: sensor-resolution-reappearance-coverage.json (gdacs-tc-1001305 still OPEN, history unchanged since 2026-09-03, no second closure); sensor-source-reconfirmation-blind-spot.json (gdacs-fl-1103815's datemodified still frozen at 2026-09-03T13:36:40 through the 2026-09-11 snapshot, a seventh consecutive frozen night since the 2026-09-08 review; the other eighteen GDACS futures in the 2026-08-19-identified echoing set are all still echoing nightly with zero exceptions, re-derived tonight from foreknown/snapshots/2026-09-06 through 2026-09-11/gdacs.json -- no second instance of a stop to add). No memoryhole verdicts: memoryhole/readings/2026-09-10.json, the newest reading, carries zero rule-layer abstentions across 31 entries. sensor-registry-stall.json's own discovery-pass-cadence gap (obs-2026-09-11-1.json) is unchanged -- last night's pass (2026-09-11) does carry a discovery-pass entry in autonomy/log.jsonl, so no new missing night to add to that observation's list.
